source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Unit 6 (PDF 93-127), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh Unit 6 (Sequences and Series) ke poore unit se practice MCQs hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah, jis mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 A systematic arrangement of numbers according to a given rule is called a:
(Kisi diye gaye qaide (rule) ke mutabiq numbers ki tarteeb-waar tarteeb ko kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Definition ke mutabiq qaide se tarteeb diye gaye numbers sequence (tarteeb) banate hain; series terms ka jama (sum) hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: A systematic arrangement of numbers according to a given rule is called a sequence

blocks.prompt:
2 If \(a_{n} = 2n^{2} - 1\), then \(a_{3}\) equals:
(Agar \(a_{n} = 2n^{2} - 1\) ho to \(a_{3}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(n = 3\) rakhein: \(a_{3} = 2(3)^{2} - 1 = 18 - 1 = 17\). (\(35\) tab aata hai jab \(2 \times 3\) ka square le liya jaye.)

book_ref.quote: it is also called the general term of the sequence

blocks.prompt:
3 In a sequence, the term just before the \(n\)th term \(a_{n}\) is written as:
(Sequence mein \(n\)th term \(a_{n}\) se foran pehle wala term kaise likha jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Position \(n - 1\) wala term \(a_{n-1}\) hai, yani \((n-1)\)st term. \(a_{n} - 1\) ka matlab hai \(n\)th term minus aik.

book_ref.quote: The terms just before it are called the

blocks.prompt:
4 The general term of the sequence \(7, 12, 17, 22, \ldots\) is:
(Sequence \(7, 12, 17, 22, \ldots\) ka general term kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har term pichle se 5 zyada hai, is liye rule mein \(5n\) hai; \(5(1) + 2 = 7\), \(5(2) + 2 = 12\).

book_ref.quote: When a set of numbers follows a pattern and there is a clear rule for finding the next number

blocks.prompt:
5 Which of the following is a finite sequence?
(In mein se kaun si finite (mehdood) sequence hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(2, 4, 6, \ldots, 40\) ka aakhri term (40) likha hai, is ke 20 terms hain, is liye finite hai; baqi kabhi khatam nahi hotin.

book_ref.quote: A sequence which consists of a finite number of terms is called a finite sequence

blocks.prompt:

(Sequence \(a_{n} = n^{2} + 2n\) ke pehle chaar terms kya hain?)

book_ref.quote: then we can find the terms of the sequence
A sequence which consists of an infinite number of terms is called an infinite sequence

blocks.prompt:

book_ref.quote: Sequences of numbers which follow specific patterns are called progressions

book_ref.quote: The \(n\)th term of an arithmetic progression can be written as:

blocks.explanation: Aakhir se \(n\)th term shuru se \((m - n + 1)\)th hota hai: \(12 - 4 + 1 = 9\).
